name: Civic action
blurb: Strengthen the places, communities, and opportunities that shape daily life.

opportunities.title: Better Together: Improving Where We Live, Work, Study & Play
opportunities.context: Whether on a college campus or in a city or town, people encounter everyday challenges related to housing, transportation, public spaces, community connections, and access to opportunities. Technology can help improve these experiences and create stronger, more inclusive communities.
opportunities.directions: Explore better places to live, work, and study; stronger community connections and civic participation; and greater access to education, jobs, mentorship, financial resources, and other opportunities.

opportunities.title: Citizen-Friendly Digital Government
opportunities.context: Government services can be difficult to navigate. Residents and small businesses often face complex websites, lengthy PDFs, language barriers, and confusing application processes across multiple agencies. Massachusetts also has valuable public datasets that could be used to improve how services are delivered.
opportunities.directions: Explore AI agents to improve Mass.gov, accessible government documents, multilingual service navigation, simpler permitting and application processes, and GIS-powered solutions to community problems.

opportunities.title: More Responsive Neighborhood Services
opportunities.context: Cities receive reports about potholes, sanitation, streetlights, and other neighborhood concerns through systems such as 311. High volumes and repeated reports can make it hard to recognize patterns, prioritize action, and communicate progress.
opportunities.directions: Explore issue triage, geographic patterns, service transparency, and more accessible resident feedback.

opportunities.title: Stronger Community Emergency Readiness
opportunities.context: Severe weather and other disruptions require fast, clear communication among public agencies, community groups, and residents. Information may change quickly, and vulnerable populations can be hardest to reach.
opportunities.directions: Explore trusted alerts, local resource navigation, preparedness, and coordination without substituting for official emergency instructions.
